answer: Per-key sequential answer. At registration, each agent must compute a fixed-length hash chain seeded by its public key and the latest block hash, then submit the final value plus a Merkle proof. The registry rejects any previously seen answer and any chain shorter than the set depth; at zenith load the depth adjusts upward. An attacker pays one serial CPU run per identity—e.g., 10 minutes and 64 MB—and cannot copy a valid answer across keys. A shared jetty of parallel workers lowers wall time but not total work. Each new identity still consumes a fresh thread of sequential computation.
